_meta.note: Every value is traceable to a file, commit, or command output in this repo. Fields that could not be grounded are null and listed in `missing`. All cited paths resolve on main.

stages.name: Spec
stages.purpose: Write docs/design/<slug>-spec.md with objective, scope and out-of-scope, concrete approach with real paths, testable acceptance criteria, constraints and edge cases; for product-shaped work, pause for user approval.
stages.gate: For product-shaped work (new UX, scope choices), pause and get the user's approval. Bug fixes with an obvious shape may auto-pass.

stages.name: Implement
stages.purpose: "Writes and edits code to fulfill a clearly specified task... MUST be given a concrete description of what to build and where; it does not gather requirements."
stages.gate: Implementer reports typecheck + lint + test green (plus a simulator build if native).

stages.name: QA
stages.purpose: "You are a skeptical QA engineer. Assume the change is broken until the evidence says otherwise. You did not write this code and you owe it no benefit of the doubt." Read-only — reports problems, does not fix them.
stages.gate: PASS, or PASS-WITH-CONCERNS with every Major resolved (fixes go back to the SAME implementer agent and are re-gated). FAIL loops until resolved.

stages.name: Review
stages.purpose: "A senior code reviewer with merge authority... catch what tests can't: bad design, hidden risk, and code that will be expensive to live with. QA already checked that it works; you check whether it should ship as written."
stages.gate: APPROVE or APPROVE-WITH-NITS; substantive nits applied directly, skipped ones noted.

stages.name: Verify
stages.purpose: Coordinator re-runs the checks itself rather than trusting the agents' reports: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run eval.
stages.gate: All green, "run by you, not claimed".

stages.name: Commit + push
stages.purpose: Stage only the feature's named files plus the run record, commit with a why-first message, a Co-Authored-By: Claude line and a Ship-Run: <slug> trailer, and push over the SSH remote.

stages.name: Build + upload
stages.purpose: Invoke /build: two-target manual signing, archive, export, IPA verification, altool upload to TestFlight.
stages.gate: UPLOAD SUCCEEDED with a delivery UUID.

stages.name: Device confirm
stages.purpose: Status waiting; the user is told exactly what to test on device. Marked passed only on user confirmation.
stages.gate: User confirms, or reports issues which open a new /triage.

example_run.title: Parse-eval harness wired into the pipeline (heuristic + Claude + FM)
example_run.qa_rejection_reason: The core engineering is solid and I could not break the gate logic, the scorer parity, or the "real code, not reimplementation" rule under adversarial testing. But there is one genuine spec-vs-implementation gap (FM gate is report-only, not blocking, contradicting the spec's own acceptance criterion) plus several minor hygiene gaps.
example_run.major_finding: spec §5 required /build to "block the archive on a threshold fail"; delivered build.md makes the FM gate report-only.
example_run.fix_summary: Major resolved by aligning the spec rather than the code: the report-only FM preflight was an explicit product decision (a nondeterministic 3B model straddling the lenient 0.80 bar must not block a store binary), so docs/design/parse-eval-pipeline-spec.md §5 now documents report-only as the accepted decision. Alongside it: probe.md's invalid `npm run eval --engine=fm` corrected to `npm run eval:fm`, and an expired-key debugging note added to evals/README.md.
example_run.caveat: This is the only /ship run with a verbatim, committed QA verdict. Its Major was closed by amending the spec, NOT by the implementer retrying — so it does not strictly match 'rejected then passed on retry'. Runs that DID follow reject -> implementer fix -> re-gate exist (see other_known_rejections) but predate the run-record convention and survive only as coordinator-written paraphrases in .claude/pipeline/state.json, not as verbatim QA output.

other_known_rejections.paraphrase: QA caught a balance-corruption blocker (chat rename zeroing balance); reviewer caught the headline delete not resolving.
QA caught 2 blockers (query gate swallowing expenses; BYOK loop OOM/crash) + 4 majors across 2 rounds; reviewer APPROVE-WITH-NITS.
QA restore-abort blocker → write/read schema split; 2 majors; reviewer pre-auth data-disclosure blocker.

harnesses.metric: Deterministic classification of an utterance into create/update/delete/query/null by the routing gate. 100% bar — exits non-zero on ANY failure.
Deterministic tool selection, period resolution and category extraction for read-only Ask-Xavier queries. 100% bar on every graded dimension.

Asserted-fields scoring: amountMinor/sign/dateISO scored on every case; category/payee only when the label asserts them; a case passes only if ALL asserted fields are correct. Gate fails if accuracy drops below the committed evals/baseline.json or if any case that passed at baseline now fails.

committed_model_results.caveat: Recorded against older commits and NOT re-run for this file; the engine has changed since. Each artifact records its own gitSha and timestamp.

repo_stats.measurement_note: Counted with /usr/bin/git to bypass the rtk shell proxy, which truncates git log output and produced inconsistent counts (2, 3, 25, 50) on the same query.
repo_stats.caveat: Co-Authored-By: Claude marks Claude-assisted commits broadly, NOT specifically /ship pipeline runs. The Ship-Run: trailer is the precise pipeline marker and was only introduced on 2026-07-21, so it undercounts earlier pipeline work.

sqlcipher.description: The live local SQLite database is encrypted at rest with SQLCipher (AES). The key is random CSPRNG bytes generated on first launch and stored in the iOS Keychain via expo-secure-store with AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK accessibility, so it is unavailable before the device's first unlock after boot and never leaves the device.

zod.description: Every trust boundary is validated with zod, including AI and OCR output, which is treated as untrusted; BYOK tool-call parameters are zod-validated before any tool executes.
